ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, two straight wires a and b placed in parallel, both with length L, are placed in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the plane in which the wires lie. When wire a carries a current intensity I, wire b carries a current intensity 2I, and the current directions are opposite, the magnitude of the magnetic field force on wire a is $F_1$, and the magnitude of the magnetic field force on wire b is $F_2$. Then the magnitude of the magnetic induction produced at wire b by the current in conducting wire a is ____.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows: two vertical parallel straight wires, the left one labeled a and the right one labeled b; the current in a is I, with the arrow upward; the current in b is 2I, with the arrow downward. Multiple “×” marks are drawn in the region where the wires are located, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. Let the magnitude of the magnetic induction of the uniform magnetic field be B0, and let the magnitude of the magnetic induction produced at wire b by the current in wire a be B. Since the magnitude of the magnetic field is proportional to the current, the current in wire b is 2I, so the magnitude of the magnetic induction produced by wire b at a is 2B. Judging by the right-hand rule according to the current directions in the figure: the direction of the magnetic field produced by a at b is inward, and the direction of the magnetic field produced by b at a is also inward; both are the same as the direction of the externally applied uniform magnetic field, so the total magnetic field magnitudes at their respective wires are added. For wire a, the magnitude of the force is F1 = I L (B0 + 2B). For wire b, the magnitude of the force is F2 = 2 I L (B0 + B). Eliminate B0: 2F1 = 2IL(B0 + 2B) = 2ILB0 + 4ILB, F2 = 2IL(B0 + B) = 2ILB0 + 2ILB, so 2F1 - F2 = 2ILB. Therefore B = (2F1 - F2)/(2IL).
